maya: heads-up — canary rollout of kernel-selector v2 hit an unexpected tail-latency regression on host-side. saw ~3x p99 on short requests (<=64 tokens).

infra-bot: deploy canary kernel-selector:v2 -> 10% of traffic at 1739991120

maya: repro sketch: small chat requests (single-turn, prompt ~40 tokens) used to avg 20ms p95. after kernel switch p95 ~60ms, p99 spiking to 180-220ms. throughput not impacted.

liam: any CPU spikes on host? or more write syscalls on grpc?

maya: profile attached (paste below). main diffs: increased writev syscalls, more small writes (~128-512B) plus extra parse latency in host preproc step. KV-cache hit rate fluctuated — more evictions around canary nodes.

sasha: can you paste the perf log? also which kernel mapping changed (attention kernel or matmul)?

maya: gist of perf (trimmed):
```
host-preproc	+34ms	parse_tokenize: 12ms -> 28ms
grpc-writev	+20ms	syscalls increase: 120/s -> 410/s
kvcache	+8ms	hitrate: 0.92 -> 0.78
kernel-selected: old=attn_opt_v1,new=attn_mem_stream_v2
```

liam: interesting — attn_mem_stream_v2 trades memory layout for steady-state throughput. Could be causing more fragment writes because we changed streaming chunk boundaries on host.

sasha: that explains increase in small writes — host fragmenter decides chunk sizes based on expected decode pipeline timing. New kernel seems to change token decode pacing -> more frequent flushes.

maya: timeline: canary started 1739991120, regression visible 1739991145. Rolling back now?

liam: let's pause canary and revert selector to v1 on affected hosts. Also capture tcpdump and host trace on a few canary instances for 1 minute.

infra-bot: rollback kernel-selector:v1 initiated by liam at 1739991150

maya: quick telemetry notes for postmortem: collect per-request
- host parse time
- socket writev sizes distribution (buckets 64,128,256,512,1k)
- kvcache get/evict counters
- kernel chosen + sequence length + decode emit rate

sasha: for immediate mitigation we can:
- increase write coalescing window in ingress proxy from 2ms -> 6ms (temporary)
- relax auto-batching heuristic: require 2x longer warmup before switching to micro-batch mode
- bump KV-cache capacity on canary hosts to avoid thrash (double local cache size)

liam: agree. but be mindful of latency tradeoffs for larger coalesce window. do it as an opt-in flag for canary only.

maya: I'll open a short issue with profiling artifacts + a small repro harness that drives short chat requests at 600rps. tagging @liam @sasha.

liam: assign to eng-runtime perf. ETA to triage and test mitigations: 2h.

sasha: we should also add a kernel-selection simulation in CI: run a micro-benchmark that checks writev distribution and kvcache hit-rate for new kernels before rollout. prevents this class of regression.

maya: noted. creating follow-ups: 1) revert canary (done), 2) collect traces, 3) test write-coalesce flag, 4) add CI microbench.

infra-bot: rollback complete at 1739991160. Canary traffic now on kernel-selector:v1

liam: thanks — let's sync in 30m in #eng-runtime if traces show anything surprising. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all. will paste traces in this thread when uploaded.
